text:
Nadia R: Spinning up a follow-up thread from yesterday's design huddle. I'm worried the current autoscale churn causes expensive prewarm churn for busy tenants. Proposal: split headroom into guaranteed + elastic buckets, and serve elastic from a regional burst pool.

Tom G: Nice. guaranteed = stable reservation that never expires quickly, elastic = short-lived spikes? How do you avoid a single tenant burning the pool?

Nadia R: Exactly. Guaranteed size = function of commit level (reserved tokens) or long-term avg usage; elastic = min(ceil(0.05 * steady_tokens), 6). Elastic leases last 60s by default, can be extended if used consecutively but capped. Global pool has per-tenant debit caps and a fairness token that enforces sliding windows.

Priya K: The fairness token sounds complex. Could we implement simpler: global pool grants only if tenant hasn't used >X% of pool in last Y mins?

Nadia R: That's a simpler rule, yes. Sliding-window quota per-tenant is fine for first pass. We can evolve to weighted fairness later.

Evan M: Implementation notes: we must not centralize at control-plane single-counter. Operator should keep a lightweight region-level counter CRD. Use optimistic updates (CAS) with backoff. If apiserver qps concerns arise, fall back to sidecar-local counters and batch-sync every 2s with rate-limit. Allow bounded oversubscribe tolerance of ~2 slots per region.

Tom G: How do sidecars handle leaderless races? occasional oversubscribe is ok, but can that violate SLOs? We need safety thresholds and alerts.

Priya K: Add a safety controller that watches observed oversubscribe events and rate-limits future grants. Also, mark a region "constrained" if oversubscribe > threshold for 30s and then reduce elastic grant rate.

Nadia R: Good. Failure modes: if operator loses control-plane connectivity, sidecars go into degraded mode (no elastic grants, only guaranteed). Emit metric headroom.degraded=1 and create alert. Also surface to Console that elastic_burst=false for the region.

ops-bot: Note: ticket INF-5254 created "regional-elastic-burst-pool + sidecar-sync"

Evan M: One more: model fallback & QoS. Instead of automatic quantization, allow per-route fallback policies: fallback_priority = [smaller-model, truncated-seq]. Only use fallback when queue latency P95 > SLO and after soft timeout. Keep logs of reason for fallback.

Tom G: Telemetry needs: region.elastic_grants, tenant.elastic_used, tenant.elastic_denied, region.oversubscribe_count, fallback.trigger_reasons, queue.wait_histogram. Also billing: record elastic_grant_id so billing pipeline can attribute bursts to tenant usage.

Priya K: On billing: do we charge elastic grants immediately or after they are used? I'd prefer charge on use, with an invoice event that references the grant_id and tokens_consumed. We need spec for PMs.

Nadia R: Agreed. Draft example config for the policy: 
```yaml
name: regional-elastic-v1
guaranteed:
  calc: 'max(reservation_slots, ceil(0.02 * steady_tokens))'  # per-tenant guaranteed
elastic:
  pct_of_steady: 0.05
  max_slots: 6
  lease_secs: 60
  extend_if_used: true
  extend_cap: 180
  per_tenant_window_limit: { slots: 24, window_secs: 600 }
region_pool:
  enabled: true
  oversubscribe_tolerance: 2
  constrained_threshold: 3  # oversubscribe events in 30s triggers constrained mode
admission:
  on_failure: { enterprise: queue, standard: queue_with_soft_timeout_30s_and_fallback, preemptible: best_effort }
```

Evan M: For the operator shim sketch: CRD shape is simple: { region, available_slots, seq } with optimistic updates. Sidecar keeps local counters and syncs diffs in batches. Add healthcheck endpoint /burst-health returning {mode: normal|constrained|degraded}.

Tom G: Can you add a small perf test to the perf harness? compare CRD-only vs sidecar-batched sync across 5 regions at 1000 tenants and 200 qps spikes. We care about apiserver qps and observed grant latency <50ms.

Nadia R: Will include that in RFC. Action items: (1) I'll open RFC with config + operator shape + failure modes, (2) Evan to prototype sidecar sync loop and health endpoint, (3) Tom to add perf tests.

Priya K: I'll draft the telemetry + billing events doc and sync with PM. Also volunteer to review RFC.

Nadia R: thanks team. quick thumbs if you support the guaranteed+elastic split and sidecar-batched approach.

Tom G: +1

Priya K: +1

Evan M: +1

Nadia R: :thumbsup: I'll post the RFC link once it's up.
